```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8)
```

## Load Libraries and Data

```{r load-libraries}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(viridis)
library(lubridate)

# Load the student-week aggregations
data <- read_csv("student_week_aggregations2.csv")

# Basic data info
cat("Data dimensions:", nrow(data), "rows,", ncol(data), "columns\n")
cat("Date range:", min(data$week_id), "to", max(data$week_id), "\n")
cat("Number of unique students:", n_distinct(data$anon_student_id), "\n")
cat("Number of unique weeks:", n_distinct(data$week_id), "\n")
```

## Data Preparation

```{r data-prep}
# Filter to students with proficiency data and reasonable activity
students_with_proficiency <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(avg_proficiency)) %>%
  group_by(anon_student_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_weeks = n(),
    avg_proficiency_overall = mean(avg_proficiency, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_weeks >= 3)  # At least 3 weeks of data

cat("Students with proficiency data and ≥3 weeks:", nrow(students_with_proficiency), "\n")

# Sample students for heatmap (to avoid overcrowding)
set.seed(42)  # For reproducibility
sample_size <- min(20, nrow(students_with_proficiency))  # Max 20 students
sampled_students <- students_with_proficiency %>%
  slice_sample(n = sample_size) %>%
  pull(anon_student_id)

cat("Sampled", length(sampled_students), "students for heatmap\n")
```

## Heatmap: Sample Students' Proficiency Across Weeks

```{r heatmap}
# Prepare data for heatmap
heatmap_data <- data %>%
  filter(anon_student_id %in% sampled_students,
         !is.na(avg_proficiency)) %>%
  # Create shorter student labels for readability
  mutate(student_label = paste0("S", match(anon_student_id, sampled_students)))

# Create heatmap
p1 <- ggplot(heatmap_data, aes(x = week_id, y = student_label, fill = avg_proficiency)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Proficiency", 
                       option = "plasma",
                       na.value = "grey90") +
  labs(
    title = "Student Proficiency Heatmap Across Weeks",
    subtitle = paste("Sample of", length(sampled_students), "students"),
    x = "Week",
    y = "Student"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12)
  )

print(p1)
```

## Box Plots: Proficiency Distribution Across Weeks

```{r boxplots}
# Prepare data for box plots - filter to weeks with sufficient data
weekly_counts <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(avg_proficiency)) %>%
  count(week_id, name = "n_students") %>%
  filter(n_students >= 5)  # At least 5 students per week

box_data <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(avg_proficiency),
         week_id %in% weekly_counts$week_id)

# Create box plots
p2 <- ggplot(box_data, aes(x = week_id, y = avg_proficiency)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(group = week_id), 
               outlier.alpha = 0.6, 
               outlier.size = 0.8,
               fill = "lightblue", 
               alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), 
              method = "loess", 
              se = TRUE, 
              color = "red", 
              size = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Student Proficiency Across Weeks",
    subtitle = "Box plots show quartiles, red line shows trend",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Average Proficiency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1))

print(p2)
```

## Summary Statistics

```{r summary-stats}
# Overall proficiency statistics
proficiency_summary <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(avg_proficiency)) %>%
  summarise(
    n_observations = n(),
    mean_proficiency = mean(avg_proficiency),
    median_proficiency = median(avg_proficiency),
    sd_proficiency = sd(avg_proficiency),
    min_proficiency = min(avg_proficiency),
    max_proficiency = max(avg_proficiency)
  )

cat("Overall Proficiency Statistics:\n")
print(proficiency_summary)

# Weekly trend summary
weekly_summary <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(avg_proficiency)) %>%
  group_by(week_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_students = n(),
    mean_proficiency = mean(avg_proficiency),
    median_proficiency = median(avg_proficiency),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(week_id)

cat("\nWeeks summary:\n")
print(n = Inf, weekly_summary)
```
